name: Green Bank Telescope
description: A fully steerable radio telescope with a 100-metre-diameter collecting area, operated by the Green Bank Observatory. It works from meter to millimeter wavelengths (0.1-116 GHz).
highlights: Frank Drake's Project Ozma, the first modern search for signals from other civilisations, was carried out at Green Bank in 1960 with an earlier 26-metre dish.
Described as the world's largest fully steerable radio telescope.
It replaced the 300-foot telescope, which collapsed in 1988.
